When you are done it is measured again: G-Eval by google/gemma-4-e2b against the competitor's best post, and Jev's not-ai-slop gate. Only a version that scores higher and that Jev calls genuine is kept; anything else is put back, so change the writing, not only the wording.

The current version (version 1) scores 0.47; the bar is 0.75.
- beats-competition 0.30: GreatFrontEnd's bar is a numbered pairs hook ('5 React pairs that sound similar, but work differently') plus a save-before-interview CTA in a scannable carousel. The actual first line is a career thesis ('If an agent took the typing part of your frontend job...') that a scroller would not stop for as readily. - human-voice 0.70: The LinkedIn post is specific to the selector claim and sources: createSelector inputs, the { ...todo, todoItems } diff, rejecting shallowEqual because filter() allocates, a toBe() guard, and the 315-minute State essentials plan with eight named docs. That work detail and the between-jobs interview opinion could not be moved to another topic unchanged. Generated-copy habits still shape it: an aphoristic reversal opener, the claim restated before the list, arrow bullets, and a One/Then/Then product cadence.
- channel-native 0.60: The LinkedIn post is not a straight twin: its claim (naming the layer and what “done” means as a test is the job left after agents write code), campaign-wrap framing, and product specifics (elegantfrontend.training, 315-minute State essentials, eight terms, practice in the first comment) are new to a reader of the selector twins. It still recycles the same examples those twins already used—createSelector, { ...todo, todoItems }, rejecting shallowEqual because filter() returns a new array, and a toBe() guardrail—and it never becomes the story-plus-document-carousel LinkedIn is supposed to rewar
- Jev: genuine (0% likely slop)

"What their best posts have in common", and the `linkedin-carousels` bar in `benzene-standards.yaml`.

- GreatFrontEnd's Page has 89,925 followers. Its 10 visible posts were aged 1 to 5 days, and their reactions ranged
  from 11 to 208.
- The openings it quotes include a series: "5 CSS animation pairs that sound similar, but work differently: Regular CSS
  transition vs @starting-style…", "5 React pairs that sound similar, but work differently … Save this before your next
  React interview" and "5 image and media pairs…".
- The report names this series as the model for our terminology carousels: it "maps 1:1 onto our glossary".

Done. I rewrote the post and added its document carousel deck.

## What I changed and why

**`linkedin-2026-10-23-name-the-boundary.md`** — full rewrite of the body, same front-matter fields (channel, date, claim, source, campaign, showcase_url) plus the required `format: document`, `slides`, `document_title`, and `first_comment`.

**Why the old version scored low:**
- Hook was a career thesis ("If an agent took the typing part of your frontend job…") that a scroller wouldn't stop for.
- No carousel/document format — the core LinkedIn format GreatFrontEnd's bar sets.
- Body recycled the twins' examples (`{ ...todo, todoItems }`, `shallowEqual`, `toBe()`, createSelector) and spent most of its length on a 315-minute course pitch instead of code/mechanism.
- Generated-copy habits: aphoristic reversal opener, claim restated before the list, arrow bullets, One/Then/Then cadence.

**What the rewrite does differently:**
- Hook in the first two lines: *"An agent writes the selector. A human names the layer it reads from."* — specific, concrete, not a topic.
- A document carousel (7 slides, 5–9 allowed) built around this post's unique claim — *naming the boundary* — not selector mechanics already covered by the 10-19, 10-20, 10-21, 10-22 twins.
- No arrow bullets, no "One/Then/Then" cadence, no claim restated before a list, no recycled `{ ...todo }` / `toBe()` / `shallowEqual` focus.
- Five terms about layers/boundaries (UI vs server state, action vs event, selector vs reducer, store vs state, done as a reference test), each with one idea and a code-relevant mechanism.
- Last slide is the CTA pointing at `elegantfrontend.training/practice/memoized-selector.html` with the correct `utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=state-selectors`.
- Showcase link lives in `first_comment` per the profile's LinkedIn showcase rule.
- 4 hashtags (3–5 allowed), ~1,765 characters (under 3,000).
- All facts sourced from `docs/_data/plans.yml` (315 minutes, eight term docs, eight practice questions), `docs/practice/memoized-selector.md` (`recomputations()`), and `docs/state/selectors.md` — no invented numbers, links, versions, or quotes.

**`slides/name-the-boundary.md`** — new deck file, one slide per `---` block, each with a `# Title` under 60 chars and body under 320 chars, last slide the CTA with the showcase URL.

The post stays held for CEO review; nothing is posted.
